correctness.rationale: For any P subset of primes 1(mod4), a_k=2^k product_{r in P,r<=k}r forms a divisibility chain with log a_k=O(k). On Q=product_{r in P,r<=sqrt(log X)}r, CRT makes 1_{r|n} independent Bernoulli(1/r) over residues, and reduced-prime-square sums independent Bernoulli(2/(r-1)). Exponential Markov bounds high T(n) and low T(p²+q²) with shared exponent delta=1-t+t log t, t=1/log2, checked independently. Q=exp(O(sqrt(log X))) allows uniform Brun-Titchmarsh for p,q<=sqrt X; shifts k or l<ceil sqrt(log X) and primes dividing Q cost O(X/sqrt(log X)). Combining disjoint cases yields the claimed uniform finite-X bound. Mertens in progression 1 mod4 yields exponent delta/2 for loglog X. Independent finite checks validate eight prime moduli, not the analytic uniform bound.
residual_risks: Bounded checking corroborates examples, not unrestricted quantified mathematics.
